subject.title: fix(lock): scope reentrancy to logical owners

question: Should `reentrantOwner` become the supported public mechanism for deliberately nested file-lock acquisition, including its synchronous API parity, rather than keeping all nested acquisition unsupported after the JSON-store fix?
rationale: The patch deliberately adds a new public behavioral contract after current main removed the unsound boolean; choosing the permanent reentrancy API and caller obligations requires maintainer intent beyond mechanical correctness.

options.title: Accept owner-scoped reentrancy
options.body: Adopt `reentrantOwner` as the documented opt-in contract, contingent on runtime proof and completed platform validation.

options.title: Keep nesting unsupported
options.body: Retain current-main serialization behavior and reject this additional public lock mode if the compatibility benefit is not worth its misuse surface.

recommendation.title: Accept owner-scoped reentrancy
recommendation.body: Adopt `reentrantOwner` as the documented opt-in contract, contingent on runtime proof and completed platform validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged serialization change on current main and the proposed follow-up, so they have the clearest recent context on the intended lock contract.
